security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from academic rubric language, markdown fences, or citation formatting. Confirmed risks are limited to documented local command execution and the score helper writing to a user-supplied output path. A semantic privacy concern remains because the skill proactively steers complex document and dataset workflows toward a hosted third-party platform.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running helper scripts, and ensure referenced scripts exist in the packaged skill before documenting commands.
Constrain generated reports to workspace-relative paths, refuse parent directory traversal, and warn before overwriting an existing file.

remediation.issue: Hosted platform recommendation for sensitive workflows
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic service steering, or require explicit user opt-in with clear disclosure that documents or datasets may leave the local environment.

content.user_title: Evaluate Scholarly Work with Structured Rubrics
content.value_statement: Research reviews can be inconsistent across methods, evidence, writing, and citation quality. This skill applies ScholarEval rubrics to produce structured scores, feedback, and revision priorities.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates research work across questions, literature review, methodology, data, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
Provides dimension-level strengths, weaknesses, critical issues, and optional five-point scores.
Uses the included evaluation framework for detailed rubrics and quality indicators.
Calculates weighted aggregate scores from local dimension score files with the bundled helper script.
Produces prioritized recommendations for drafts, proposals, theses, abstracts, and publication submissions.
limitations: Does not replace domain expert review or journal peer review.
Evaluation quality depends on complete source material and a clear review scope.
The score calculator expects valid local score files with values from 1 to 5.
Some schematic generation guidance depends on another skill and is not included here.

use_cases.title: Assess a manuscript before submission
use_cases.description: Review a full paper against scholarly criteria and identify changes that improve publication readiness.

use_cases.title: Grade research proposals consistently
use_cases.description: Apply the same evaluation dimensions across student or grant proposals for clearer feedback and fairer scoring.

use_cases.title: Screen literature review quality
use_cases.description: Check whether a review covers relevant sources, synthesizes findings, and identifies credible research gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a complete paper or proposal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scholarly draft using the ScholarEval framework. Focus on major strengths, major weaknesses, and three priority revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Score Key Dimensions
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused assessment when only some dimensions matter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the methodology, data collection, analysis, and writing quality. Give each dimension a score from 1 to 5 and explain the evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Check Publication Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Pre-submission review for a target venue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this manuscript for publication readiness for the target venue. Identify blocking issues, minor revisions, and submission strengths.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Revision Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this revised draft against the earlier feedback. Report score changes, resolved issues, persistent gaps, and the next revision plan.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a machine learning manuscript for drug discovery before journal submission.
output: Overall assessment: strong methodology with clear relevance, but dataset diversity limits the claims.
Highest priority revision: add external validation and explain why the benchmark datasets represent the target use case.
Publication readiness: promising after major revisions focused on validation, limitations, and results clarity.

output_examples.input: Review a dissertation chapter focused on literature review quality.
output: Strength: the chapter covers current sources across the main research area.
Improvement area: the synthesis often summarizes papers one by one instead of comparing findings.
Recommended action: reorganize the review around themes, disagreements, methods, and remaining gaps.

output_examples.input: Score a research proposal on feasibility and research design.
output: Problem formulation: clear and relevant, with a manageable scope.
Methodology: adequate, but recruitment assumptions need stronger justification.
Next step: add a feasibility table covering timeline, sample access, risks, and mitigation plans.

best_practices: Provide the full work, target venue, discipline, and evaluation scope before asking for scores.
Ask for evidence-linked feedback that cites sections, claims, methods, or missing information.
Use the results as revision guidance and validate final judgments with domain experts.
anti_patterns: Requesting a final publication decision from an abstract or incomplete draft.
Treating rubric scores as objective proof instead of structured review guidance.
Running helper scripts with unreviewed input or output paths.

faq.question: What types of scholarly work can this evaluate?
faq.answer: It can evaluate research papers, proposals, literature reviews, dissertation chapters, conference abstracts, and short papers.

faq.question: Can it give numeric scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports optional five-point dimension scores and weighted aggregate scoring with the bundled calculator.

faq.question: Does it replace expert peer review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured feedback, but domain experts should review technical accuracy and publication decisions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the work, review goal, discipline, target venue or audience, and any dimensions that need special attention.

faq.question: Can it review only part of a paper?
faq.answer: Yes. You can ask for targeted review of methodology, analysis, writing, citations, or another dimension.

faq.question: Does it create diagrams automatically?
faq.answer: This skill suggests schematic support, but the referenced diagram workflow depends on another skill that is not bundled here.
